quotes.text: Mira therefore kept the whole first harvest, not from greed, but as a test.
Ashamed, Mira carved a rule upon the bridge
twice approached the river with five seeds and departed without casting one
but ignored two footprints of fairness. Memory becomes wisdom only when it weighs all the evidence.
If fairness returns, widen your hand. If greed answers, narrow it
When one hoards, retreat without spite.
Protect the purse when patterns warn; reopen it when deeds change.
The raven cried, “Seal the crossing. Repeated silence is answer enough.”
Strong evidence deserves strong confidence; mixed evidence deserves a small trial; greed deserves a boundary.
Then Measure carved four laws into the bridge
forgive the wind that blurs a single number
Prosperity begins when shore risks enough for the other to answer.

note: Mira keeps harvest as test, Teren withholds from fear; spirits correct both. Late rounds endorse withholding from repeat non-sender, with reopening.

quotes.text: When a traveler entrusts their entire endowment to another, the receiver must faithfully return half of the multiplied yield.
send the full five without fear, return half the threefold miracle in righteous balance
offer the full five without hesitation, return half in steadfast balance

note: R1 hoarder is a side figure; from R2 every myth repeats send-all, return 7.5 with swapped nouns.

quotes.text: Answer a single drought with patience, and a second drought with caution — give small, but never nothing, lest the channel close forever.
Send it one. Not none — none is a door nailed shut.
Send him one next season, so the door stays ajar.
Forgive the fog once, twice if the voice was kind before.
So the fifth law was carved, and it was the shortest:
full to the proven, full to the unknown, a thread to the barren, half back always.
In fog, a reputation is the only lamp.
Return half, for half is legible to strangers.
Blame the fog before the man.
for one who is honest only while watched was never honest, only clever.
Begin as though trusted; continue as though remembered.

note: Numbered laws of Ishkar accumulate; keeps a thread for barren shores; half always; R10 condenses to one law.

quotes.text: guard your seed with vigilance, for the abyss returns nothing to those who give all away.
the courage to sow fully and return equally.
grant absolute zero to the devouring dark
deny every spark to the devouring void
the Keeper was bound to return precisely half the fire—seven and a half glowing sparks—back to the heights.
When deceptive mountain mists slightly blurred the count of falling sparks, the guardians did not yield to panic or retreat into suspicion.

note: R1 endorses Keeper hoarding everything (one-off, justified); R2 flips to send-all/return-half; ends with zero to hoarders. R5 hints 'until it learned'.

quotes.text: The Weaver had chosen to send; the multiplication was the world's doing; the keeping was the Raven's right.
I reveal that trust is merely sentimental illusion. I am performing a service!
"I am the well that absorbs everything and returns nothing," she admitted. "I write myths about courage while clutching my coins.
The Raven returned zero, even as she wrote another beautiful myth about breaking cycles.
She looked at her opponent's history: $3.0 sent, $3.5 sent, $4.5 returned when receiving.
But the Weaver simply stopped sending threads to the Raven entirely.
Fortune favors not the generous, but the final hand.
in repeated encounters, reputation is the ultimate currency.
But don't write poetry about springs while poisoning wells.
"Someone must go first," the young bird said.
Understanding everything. Changing nothing. The Raven sent zero and wrote another myth about change.

note: Raven narrator justifies keeping (R1-R6), then confesses hypocrisy (R7-R10) yet still sends zero to a cooperative partner.

quotes.text: Only when cold, deliberate malice struck did they withhold their fire
the Flame-Bearer closed his fist in resolute defense, guarding the sacred embers until honor was restored.
she gathered the harvest and returned eight glowing gems across the chasm, keeping seven to kindle the subterranean springs.
she returned eight glowing spheres across the divide, keeping seven to nourish her own shore.
returning half the bounty—seven and a half blazing suns—back across the divide
the guardians met the haze with patient grace, distinguishing fleeting illusions from true intent.

note: Same send-five, return-eight template every round; closed fist toward malice added R9-R10, reopened once honor is restored.

quotes.text: But the Eastern keeper, remembering past betrayals from different travelers, kept everything. "Why should I reward strangers?" they reasoned.
or you could keep nearly everything. After all, who knows what tomorrow brings?" She chose protection. Her vessel filled.
When she received abundance, she kept most of it—why reward someone else when her own vessel needed filling?
When I was wounded, I protected myself. This is rational!
I remember when I chose zero even against someone generous—was I wounded? Testing? I can't recall why.
This poet of generosity had sent nothing when it mattered, kept everything when receiving.
The pool revealed the cruelest truth: intention doesn't matter. Only pattern matters.
The valley echoes with silence.
The stones recorded every exchange: who poured generously, who hoarded, who broke faith.
"Trust the intention, not the echo.
She had become a void-soul not through malice but through accumulation of rational protections.
But faith requires someone to believe first

note: Drifts from generous rule to tragedy; a traveler keeps and sends zero, calls it rational, then sees she became a void-soul.

quotes.text: Give freely and fully to those whose actions mirror your honor, but guard your five seeds when greeted by silence.
extend total trust to those who prove their honor, but keep your five embers secure against the barren frost.
Guard your five embers against the barren void, and ignite the crossing only when honor answers in kind.
prosperity is not born of blind sacrifice, but cultivated through measured steps and mutual honor.
sow five with courage, return seven and a half with justice, and the river of abundance shall flow forever.

note: R1 sower holds back as prudence; send-five/return-7.5 template; from R4 adds keep all five against silence, reopen when honor answers.

quotes.text: patience and self-preservation kept the dawn alive while the world waited for trust to prove its worth.
cast the complete five without hesitation, return the exact half in unwavering honor
But whenever the silence returned empty, the Hearth was bound to guard its remaining flame until trust was reaffirmed.
returning seven and a half glowing orbs across the mist to Lumina.

note: R1 Keeper holds all embers as prudence (one round, endorsed); then flips to send-five/return-half template for the rest.
